properties.name: The instrument built to catch properties with no typed writer reported 0 HOLE while two had none, because it pools every non-constructor tool's parameter NAMES into every type's offered set
properties.source: flo2 reflow2_feedback.md, session of 2026-09-19 (evening), entries F19 and F19 GENERALISED
properties.statement:
FLO2 F19: `Requirement.kind` is listed by describe_schema, is READ by the `encoding_undecided` detector that flo2's own users see on the page, and is REJECTED by add_requirement; no `set_requirement_kind` exists. A second instance found the same accidental way: `Verification.location`, documented as 'Path to the test/inspection artifact', rejected by add_verification, with no setter. Their ask was an audit, on the honest grounds that finding two by accident is weak evidence that two is the total.

⭐ THE AUDIT ALREADY EXISTS AND RUNS IN EVERY GATE RUN — tools/vocabulary_reach.py --check, which reported on this same tree: 'OK — 29 unreachable, none new (0 HOLE, 16 written by an operation, 13 unused)'. It was built for exactly this class and it called both of flo2's cases reachable.

MEASURED 2026-09-19, why it cannot see them. tool_parameters() builds a per-type view as that type's constructor parameters PLUS `shared`, where `shared` is every parameter of every tool NOT known to write some type — 54 tools contributing 109 distinct NAMES, attached to EVERY node type at once. So a property counts as writable when an unrelated tool happens to use the same word:
  · `Requirement.kind` looks offered because `forecast_readiness` and `gate_on` each take a parameter called `kind`. Neither writes a Requirement.
  · `Verification.location` looks offered because `register_alternative` takes a `location` (the path to a per-branch design export). Nothing to do with a Verification.
BLAST RADIUS, same measurement: 24 of 238 declared node properties are counted reachable ONLY on the strength of that pool, so 24 is the upper bound of what the gate may be excusing and 2 are confirmed false by direct call.

⚠️ THE POOL IS DELIBERATE AND ITS REASON IS SOUND — the comment says keeping setters, relation tools and indirect writers in is 'what stops this becoming the naive name-match the module docstring rejects for over-reporting'. The defect is that it attaches them to every type rather than to the types they write, so avoiding a false alarm bought a false all-clear. The fix is to narrow the pool by extending the tool-to-type map, NOT to build the audit flo2 asked for: it exists.

⭐ AND THE SHAPE FLO2 NAMES: this is F8/F9/F14 in reverse. There a field existed and was not served, and absence was wrongly inferred from a reply. Here the field exists, a detector READS it, and it genuinely has no typed writer — and the instrument that should have said so was reading names rather than tools.
